openesm.sampling_scheme: 8x semi-random with at least 45 minutes between surveys
openesm.participants: Dutch undergraduate students using social media

reference: Johannes, N., Meier, A., Reinecke, L., Ehlert, S., Setiawan, D. N., Walasek, N., Dienlin, T., Buijzen, M., & Veling, H. (2021). The relationship between online vigilance and affective well-being in everyday life: Combining smartphone logging with experience sampling. Media Psychology, 24(5), 581-605.

date.tz_evidence: The paper (Procedure) sends eight surveys a day between 09:00 and 21:00 local time. As written, the stamps run 08-19h UTC before the 2018-03-25 DST change (09-20 CET) and 07-18h after it (09-20 CEST), shifting by exactly the hour true UTC stamps would; time_survey holds local midnight converted to UTC (23:00Z before the change, 22:00Z after). So the Z stamps are true UTC.

tables.name: johannes_2021_mood
tables.instrument: Short mood scale (Wilhelm & Schoebi, 2007), six bipolar items, plus a depressed-happy item added by the authors
tables.description: Experience sampling, 8 prompts a day between 09:00 and 21:00 for 5 working days, 77 Dutch undergraduate students: seven bipolar mood items after 'At this moment, I feel:' (tired-awake, content-discontent, agitated-calm, full of energy-without energy, unwell-well, relaxed-tense, depressed-happy). 1..7; discontent, without_energy and tense run towards the negative pole.

tables.dict_note: One participant (id 66 in openESM's copy) is excluded: a technical fault sent them 69 prompts, 11 to 16 a day and often under the study's 45-minute minimum spacing, and the authors judged those data untrustworthy. The participant the paper excluded for answering too few surveys is kept.

itemtext.why: No item text for this PR, per #3421.

notes: date is when the prompt was sent (scheduled_time), not when it was answered: the data hold no answer time stamp. time_prompt equals scheduled_time, and time_survey is only the date (local midnight). Prompt time plus reactibility_survey would give an opening time, but 17 of those delays are negative, so it is not used.

Person 66 is dropped (EXCLUDE_IDS); person 51 is kept. The paper recruited 111 and kept the 77 with complete logging and survey data, which are openESM's 77; it then analysed 75. Person 66 received 69 surveys (11 to 16 a day) because of technical problems, and the authors excluded the data as untrustworthy; all 27 prompts in the data that come less than 45 minutes after the previous one (the study's minimum spacing) are person 66's. That is a broken protocol, not an analysis choice, so IRW drops them too (ruled on #3674). Person 51 answered 6 surveys, under the preregistered minimum of 8 (20% of 40); that is an analysis choice, and IRW ships the deposited data, so person 51 stays.
Responses are as given: discontent, without_energy and tense run towards the negative pole and are not reversed. The paper averages all seven into one affective well-being index.

Item text: none for this PR (#3421). For whoever does item text later: the study ran in English (participants had to be proficient in English), so openESM's wording is the original, matching the paper and the deposit's codebook.

For the openESM report (#1698): 0051_johannes's counter (and beep within a day) count backwards in time, exactly reversing the scheduled_time order, and its day column is the weekday (1 = Monday), not the study day.

flags.what: `wave` = each person's prompts numbered in scheduled_time order (openESM time columns, best first: ['scheduled_time', 'time_prompt', 'time_survey']). `date` = scheduled_time as Unix seconds. Data run 2018-02-26 08:15 .. 2018-05-24 18:05 as written. Set date.window from the paper's collection period.
flags.resolution: wave = each person's prompts numbered in time order of scheduled_time; date = scheduled_time in Unix seconds, the time the prompt was sent (no answer time stamp exists; see coding notes). date.window is the paper's recruitment period, 'between February and September 2018', ending at the preregistered stop date of 1 September 2018; the data run 2018-02-26 to 2018-05-24.

flags.what: Time zone of scheduled_time. Written with a `Z`, but in 0072_neubauer and 0056/0057_ryvkina the `Z` stamps are local time. Hour-of-day counts as written: 7h:156, 8h:216, 9h:234, 10h:220, 11h:203, 12h:269, 13h:227, 14h:238, 15h:257, 16h:238, 17h:208, 18h:259, 19h:103. No Unix time column to check against: compare with the paper. Set date.tz to 'UTC' if the stamps are true UTC, or to the study's IANA zone (e.g. 'Europe/Berlin') if they are local time, and say how you know in date.tz_evidence.
flags.resolution: UTC: see date.tz_evidence (one-hour shift at the DST change, matching a 09:00-21:00 local window).

flags.what: Tables are a first guess from file order, response scale, source, prompts asked at, and column-name prefixes. Read the codebook and split or merge so each table is one instrument or subscale (datastandard.md, 'One file per scale'); rename each `<author>_<year>_<construct>`, and set `script` to the record's name.
flags.resolution: One table, johannes_2021_mood: the seven items of the codebook's WellBeing_ block, all after 'At this moment, I feel:', which the paper (Measures, State affective well-being) describes as six Wilhelm & Schoebi (2007) mood dichotomies plus an added depressed-happy item, averaged into one index. The plan's split of happy into a separate table did not match the block. The three state online vigilance items are left out (one item per dimension, analysed separately, different anchors on salience), as are stressed, the salience/valence single items and social_pressure_phone; reasons in not_shipped.

flags.resolution: prompt_duration, reactibility_survey and concentrated_activity_binary go to not_shipped: a survey duration, a logged delay, and a filter question.
